# Nexus — Angular Micro Frontend Platform

> An open-source Angular 19 micro frontend platform built on Native Federation. Zero-config federation, live remote registration, one-command local dev, cross-team component catalog, and zero-downtime deploys — all out of the box. MIT-licensed. Developed by Bimo.

Nexus solves the operational layer that Native Federation alone does not provide: a persistent registry with WebSocket broadcast, automatic remote self-registration, an admin portal, a cross-team component catalog, a hot-reload dev proxy, and a zero-downtime cache strategy baked into nginx. A product team writes Angular components; Nexus handles everything else.

## Services

- [Gateway](https://nexus.bimo.dk/services/gateway): Public entry — nginx reverse-proxy + minimal Angular shell
- [Registry](https://nexus.bimo.dk/services/registry): Source of truth — Node/Express + WebSocket broadcast
- [Portal](https://nexus.bimo.dk/services/portal): Admin UI — dashboard, metrics, remote CRUD, component catalog
- [Host](https://nexus.bimo.dk/services/host): Layout shell that federates remotes at runtime
- [Remotes](https://nexus.bimo.dk/services/remotes): Angular remote template and self-registration pattern
- [Dev proxy](https://nexus.bimo.dk/services/proxy): Hot-reload proxy — one remote local, everything else staging
- [Base image](https://nexus.bimo.dk/services/base-image): Shared Docker base layer for all services

## Packages

- [@bimo-dk/nexus-runtime](https://nexus.bimo.dk/packages/nexus-runtime): `provideNexusHost`, `provideNexusRemote`, `nexusRoute`, `<nexus-component>`, `DynamicNexusService`, `ComponentLoaderService`, `CatalogService`
- [@bimo-dk/nexus-build](https://nexus.bimo.dk/packages/nexus-build): `@NexusRemote()` decorator, `@NexusComponent()` decorator, `nexus-build` CLI, `federation.config.json` generator
- [@bimo-dk/nexus-cli](https://nexus.bimo.dk/packages/nexus-cli): `bnx` CLI — `bnx dev`, `bnx generate remote`, `bnx publish`, `bnx status`, `bnx health`
- [@bimo-dk/nexus-core](https://nexus.bimo.dk/packages/nexus-core): Shared types, constants, `NexusRuntimeConfig`, `RemoteConfig`
- [@bimo-dk/nexus-client](https://nexus.bimo.dk/packages/nexus-client): Node.js registry client for server-side tooling and CI pipelines
- [@bimo-dk/nexus-ui](https://nexus.bimo.dk/packages/nexus-ui): Shared Angular UI components used by the host template and portal
- [@bimo-dk/nexus-testing](https://nexus.bimo.dk/packages/nexus-testing): Test utilities, mock registry, `MockNexusModule`

## Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Bimo-dk/nexus-example.git
cd nexus-example
cp .env.example .env
# Set NEXUS_TOKEN and NODE_AUTH_TOKEN (GitHub PAT, read:packages scope)
docker compose up --build
# Application:  http://localhost:8668
# Admin portal: http://localhost:8669
```

## Key concepts

**`@NexusRemote({ exposeAs: 'MyPage' })`** — Decorator on the entry component of a remote. At build time, `nexus-build` reads this decorator and writes `federation.config.json`. At runtime, `SelfRegisterService` reads it to build the registration payload sent to the registry. The `exposeAs` value must match the key in `federation.config.json`'s `exposes` block.

**`@NexusComponent({ title, category, tags, inputs })`** — Catalog metadata decorator. At build time, generates `catalog.json` next to `remoteEntry.json`. The portal's `/catalog` page and `CatalogService` aggregate these from all registered remotes.

**`provideNexusHost({ configDefaults })`** — Single Angular provider that wires up a host application. Registers an `APP_INITIALIZER` that fetches remotes from the registry, opens the WebSocket, and registers routes — no manual initialization code needed.

**`provideNexusRemote({ entry, configDefaults })`** — Single Angular provider that wires up a remote application. At bootstrap, `SelfRegisterService` POSTs the remote to the registry using metadata from the `@NexusRemote` decorator on the `entry` class.

**`nexusRoute({ path, remote, expose })`** — Returns a standard Angular `Route` with `loadComponent` that uses `ComponentLoaderService` to resolve the federated component. Lazy-loaded, cached, registry-aware.

**`<nexus-component remote="..." expose="..." [inputs]="{...}" />`** — Drop-in Angular component that loads, caches and renders any federated component by name. Handles loading and error states. Import `NexusComponent` from `@bimo-dk/nexus-runtime`.

**Three-layer fallback** — When the registry is unreachable: 1) live registry API, 2) `sessionStorage` cache from last successful fetch, 3) static backup JSON at `staticBackupUrl`.

**Self-registration** — Remotes register themselves at container startup via `provideNexusRemote`. Set `REGISTRY_INTERNAL_URL`, `NEXUS_TOKEN`, `PUBLIC_URL` and `UPSTREAM_URL` in the container's environment. No manual `bnx publish` needed in production.

**Zero-downtime cache strategy** — Gateway nginx sets `Cache-Control: no-store` on `remoteEntry.json` and `chunk-*.js`. New bundles are visible the instant a new container starts. No service worker, no cache-busting hash needed.

## Compared with alternatives

| | Nexus | Plain Native Federation | Build-time monorepo |
|---|---|---|---|
| Independent deploys | yes | yes | no |
| Runtime add/remove remotes | yes (registry + WebSocket) | no | no |
| Zero-downtime cache strategy | yes (nginx no-store) | manual | n/a |
| Cross-team component discovery | yes (catalog) | no | in-repo only |
| Local dev one remote against staging | yes (bnx dev) | manual | n/a |
| Admin UI | yes (portal) | no | no |
| Vendor lock-in | none (MIT) | none | none |
